heading: Monday, December 8, 2025
topLine: 2 stories on AI and open problems: Equational Theories Project write-up and Erdős #1026 via humans and AI. Also: Z.ai releases GLM-4.6V vision models with native tool calling.

items.headline: Equational Theories Project reports all 22 million magma implications settled in Lean
items.summary: Tao's Equational Theories Project began in September 2024 and settled all 22,028,942 implications among 4,694 equational laws for magmas. The main goal was reached on 14 April 2025, and the write-up was posted on 8 December 2025. Results came from a mix of human proofs and automated tools, including automated theorem provers, and were validated in Lean. The 36-author paper describes it as a pilot for large-scale, machine-assisted collaboration.

image.alt: Hasse diagram of equational laws implied by E854

items.headline: Erdős Problem #1026 solved through a mix of online collaboration and AI tools
items.summary: Terence Tao described how Erdős Problem #1026, on monotone subsequence sums, was resolved. On 7 December, Aristotle autonomously produced a Lean proof of the key case c(k²) = 1/k. Tao then used AlphaEvolve to find numerical upper bounds for small n, from which humans extracted the general formula, and humans also supplied proofs and constructions. Deep-research tools helped find related papers. The square case later turned out to appear already in a 2016 paper by Tidor, Wang and Yang. The general formula rests on an LLM-assembled argument that had not yet been formalized.

image.alt: Diagram of the coin-splitting game behind Erdős #1026

items.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-4.6V vision models with native tool calling
items.summary: GLM-4.6V (106B) and GLM-4.6V-Flash (9B) are MIT-licensed vision-language models with a 128K context window and native function calling, so images can be passed directly to tools. The Flash variant targets local, low-latency deployment.
